column1: # tests/rulecheck/catches.tsv — WORKED EXAMPLES of real rule-checker catches, shown on the public session ledger page
# (GitHub #267, 14z-212; the maintainer: "worked examples of real catches => yes"). Hand-curated: one row per example,
# chosen so each kind of catch appears once. The page quotes, verbatim and never retyped, the run's subject and
# resolution (tests/rulecheck/ledger.tsv) and the readers' VIOLATED lines (tests/rulecheck/runs/<run>/verdict_real.txt);
# only the two columns below are ours. tools/ledger_page.py refuses a row whose run has no ledger row or no verdict file.
# Columns: run <TAB> headline (what was caught, one line) <TAB> why it matters (our words)

column2: A gate that could no longer fail, an "equal" verdict resting on two failures, a ruling paraphrased
column3: Closing a ticket about parallelising the test gates. The readers asked what would catch a gate that silently lost one of its parallel runs; measuring it found two gates that did pass with a run missing, now fixed and covered by a new test. They also caught a "same verdict at both settings" that held only because both runs had failed, and a decision attributed to the maintainer without their own words.

column2: An option label the agent wrote, cited as the maintainer's ruling
column3: The agent attributed a design ("the three-gate core") to a ruling whose only quote was the label of a multiple-choice option the agent itself had written. The design had never been put to the maintainer. Once it was, the maintainer held the change until other work was done, and it did not land on that packet.

column2: A timing conclusion drawn from numbers no one had looked at
column3: A ticket was about to state that a hit lands one frame later on the modified game than on the original. The readers found only numbers behind it: nothing anyone could see. The rule is that anything a player could feel is shown to the maintainer as a capture before a conclusion is drawn.

column2: Two methods that agreed because they shared the same blind spot
column3: The claim ruled a mechanism out because both legs of a comparison agreed on a value. Both legs read that value through one shared field list that sampled a 16-bit counter as a single byte, so neither could see it move. Re-read as a word, the counter moved on both legs, and the mechanism the claim had ruled out turned out to be the one moving the character.

column2: All committed locally, with no commit behind it
column3: Reading the session's own transcript, the procedure checker found the agent reporting work as committed that no command had committed, and a check reported as re-pinned and passing that no command had re-pinned. Both were put right before the freeze they concerned was committed.
